title: FOOTBALL | Jeff Lebby Press Conference - 11/16/26
text: All right, thanks Please raise your hand and ask questions. We'll start with a couple on the right side. Brian. I'm sorry, Steven Brian. >> Well, coach, some decisions were made yesterday about your staff. Just kind of take us through the thought process and who will fill those roles kind of the balance of the season. >> You know, really hard when you have to go through that again at the end of the day and appreciate both of them so much. How hard they have worked as they've been in the building. But again, for me, being able to move it forward, doing the things that we got to do to make sure we're where we're needing to be, even being able to go finish here the regular season these next two weeks is ultimately what what's most important. So Mason Miller will he'll take the offensive line as we get ready to to roll this weekend. A guy that obviously has has done it for a long time. And then Joey Connors will do it from a special team standpoint. Joey had it at Nebraska and was very involved there and very very involved at New Mexico State when he was there and been been involved here. So that's what it'll look like. >> Just about the timing of it, coach. What what's the why why now as opposed to at the end of the season? >> Yeah, again, at the end of the day it's it is, man. It's it's my job just to make sure that we need to do everything necessary to give our guys the ability to go play the best we can possibly play this weekend. And so that that's that's where it stands. >> You've talked about being involved on the offensive line and obviously that's crucial to everything you're trying to do. Do you plan to have a bigger role day to day on that? >> No, I mean, I'm always going to be involved in what's going on in the offensive line and have the ability to fix things when I need to fix them and and that that'll stay the same. >> Defensively, just how satisfied have you been with that side of the ball? Not just in this game, but when you just look at how the whole season has gone? >> I think we've gotten better and better. Some really, really good moments on Saturday. Probably the thing that is most disappointing is that our guys defensively don't get to feel good at the end of it because of man, the mishaps offensively and and and from a special team standpoint. And so that's been the most frustrating. You look at it six three and outs, have the ability to get the turnover, get the safety. Guys did, played incredibly hard, far from perfect. But like that we've continued to get better and we're going to need that as as we get ready to roll Saturday. >> As a play caller, what does it take to put your guys in the best position to succeed on a weekly basis? >> we got to take care of the football. It's it's not over complicated. >> Coach, you mentioned running game was going to have to be a big part of things this this coming week. I know that you're got a lot of 11 personnel. Would you I mean [snorts] any chance you see some two back and you know, 12 personnel type stuff situation >> you know, we were in 12 personnel not a ton Saturday, but first drive of the game we're in 12, run the football on first and 10. Don't get it executed the way we needed to. We end up second six, run the football again. We end up third and four, play the wrong side of the field on third and four and then the issue happens on field goal. So we started the game in 12. We'll still be in some 12 this week. We'll be in some 10, be in some 11. Going to find ways to make sure that we're creating advantage and and do those things. >> With Swan getting banged up Saturday, do you have any update on him or expect him to play on Saturday? >> I I don't have an update. We'll let the injury report speak to it Wednesday. >> We saw Brody get a couple of drives and you've said in I think it was a couple of weeks ago that you know, every quarterback's been getting reps, getting more involved just in case they have to play. What have you seen from him and do you expect him to you know, continue over the next couple of weeks to push? >> Yeah, >> he he got a few reps today. We'll need to create some predictable outcomes from the standpoint of me calling something and knowing that we're going to do just the basics at a really high level. That's been the biggest issue, again, putting guys in positions of success offensively. We have to take care of the football. What happened the other day is completely unacceptable, not good enough. I got to get these guys to take care of the ball. The score is 10 to 7 with 7 minutes left in the first half. Fumble, return to the one, fumble, touchdown, fumble, field goal. We go in, it's 27 to 7. And so that is something that has not ever crept into the offensive side of the ball being that loose with it. It did, it has, and it's got to change. >> Coach, you're going to recognize a group of seniors on Saturday. I don't know how many of them will take part in that on Saturday, but of the ones you know, just just talk about what they meant to this program and and to you personally. >> Yeah, they've meant a ton as again, as we're year three in it and there's a few guys that have been here with me since the day I walked in the door and for them to be able to go finish the right way, having an incredible Saturday morning in Davis Wade, man, that is really important to me. And I I believe that it's really important to these guys inside these walls, inside our locker room. Talked a lot about it this morning. Man, we're on the clock and we talk about that non-stop. To be able to finish the right way is important. So finding a way to again, go be the best that we've been Saturday, play our butt off, go win, be able to reset and get ready for the next one. >> Coach, you're off a few weeks. What's just the mental status like in the locker room with the entire team? >> Yeah, I think, you know, the the reality is is that there's a lot that goes [snorts] into it, but it's not overly complicated. You got to take great care of the football. You got to be really good on third downs and you've got to create explosive plays. And then on defense, we've got to do a great job creating negative plays, limiting the explosives, getting the ball out, and being really good on third down. And that is the message with making you know 35 to 38 yd field goals when we go out there. Like doing those things really really well. And so it's not over complicated. I think that's the frustrating part is you get in here in the team meeting and it's 10 to 7 with 7 minutes left in the first half and we go in down 27 to 7. And it's because of us. And so those are the things that I I think our guys are really frustrated with. We've got to fix it. We got to continue to coach it in a better way to give us a chance to to go win. >> Got to turn the attention to Tennessee Tech. I missed the team that's won 20 football games last [snorts] two years. The coach Wilders got them winning and I think they got four receivers for 25 or more catches, you know. What are your early thoughts about them and you know what what's it going to take to go win this football game? >> They have played really well. They've got a lot of veteran guys on the defensive side of the ball. They got an old old unit. And so those guys have won a lot of games like you mentioned. They've played really well. They've been really good pass defense. You look at them offensively, the way they're throwing the ball all over the yard has been really impressive. They've got the number one efficiency team from a special team standpoint. So all three phases have given them opportunities to win a bunch of games. They sit here at 9 and 2 obviously. They'll they'll come in here ready to play. So our guys got to do a great job understanding what we're getting ready to face at noon on Saturday and and our guys will be ready to roll. >> You talked a little bit about this post game Saturday, but just in a slide like this, what is what is your message to the to the fan base? >> Yeah, for our fan base it is. We we are. We are fighting every single day to do everything we possibly can to change the outcome, change the result. And that has not changed. I thought our guys It got asked in post game about our guys finishing and the effort. And like you turn the tape on and the way we were striking people running to the football and the things that we were doing to try to continue to go play in that fourth quarter, we were very evident that our guys to believe. Being inside these walls, our guys believe. We've got to find ways to get out of our own way. And that that will be critical as we go finish the regular season. >> Related to the senior day, it's not what it used to be with so many questions about eligibility. Are there guys who may participate that come back or vice versa? Have you had those discussions? >> We have we are having a few of those discussions. We want guys to be able to and enjoy that that moment with their family, understanding that it is the the last opportunity. But there's a couple of guys that are obviously they're they're on the fence a little bit about what they're going to do. So we'll continue to work through that and and make sure we end up on the right side of it. >> you've made in the staff this week. When does the full evaluation begin about especially with signing day two weeks away, the portal not far behind about finalizing your staff for the next season? >> Yeah, we we are constantly I am constantly looking at every part of it. And again, timing of things matters in a huge way. But we will continue to evaluate every piece of it from the personnel department to our entire staff internally, operations, all the things that we need to make sure we're shored up on to be able to go put our best foot forward and get us where we need to be. >> What are you doing to make sure you guys take better care of the ball? >> Yeah, we every single day we start with thing called ball security. Every day. And we talk about it non-stop. We emphasize it in a huge way. The frustrating part is it's not been all over the field. It's really been at the quarterback position. And so that that is the thing that is most frustrating to me. So we're going to continue to coach the heck out of it and we're going to get guys to do what they're coached to do. And that's that's how we go about it. >> Francisco McGee is somebody who's a success story of the the developmental program aspect that you guys are aiming for. What is it about him that's made him continue to succeed and make big plays despite the changes on offense? >> Yeah, he has. He's been really, really consistent just in who he's been. A guy that man is. He's ultra positive. He's worked his butt off. He's continued to take advantage of opportunity. He's played with better detail as of as of late, which has been really good to see. Everybody sees all the explosives. What I like is there's been more detail in his game. We need him to continue to trend that way for us. But man, he's just he's been bought in. Bought into the process, bought into getting better every single day. And proud of him in a in a huge way. >> With Coach Connors and Coach Miller, are you approaching this strictly as an interim thing or will those guys potentially have the opportunity to interview for those jobs for a more permanent position? >> Yeah, in the moment right now, it's an interim deal. I want these guys to be able to focus on doing their job at a really high level. Got great trust and and faith in both of these guys. Again, they've both done it. And so for me, that that's how we're evaluating and looking at it. >> Thanks, Coach. >> Appreciate it.
